details.detail: Sidewall panels and seams: smooth satin off-white, with a seam mid-pier every second window running from dado to bin line. The seam spacing matches y_47303 (lines about 2 pitches apart) and sp_py_13. The wall renders #e3e6e8 at the window belt. Photos show #bdb8b3 (sp_py_13, night) and #b5bdce (py_37301), so the wall is right relative to the photo exposure.

Window recess proportions: this is the signature 777 look and it is off. In the photos the recess is about 0.80 of the window pitch wide and about 2.35x as tall as wide, with the pane bezel in its LOWER part. It runs about 0.40 m above the bezel top, up to the bin line, and about 0.24 m below the bezel. The render is 0.73 pitch wide and about 1.95x as tall as wide, with 0.20 m above and 0.11 m below the bezel. The result is a squat, centred frame.

Bezel roll-in, grey tunnel lining and 10x15 pane: a soft outer lip, a rounded-rect opening, a grey lining necking to the glass. Matches the sp_py_24 close-up (bezel #c7c0ab, lining #6c6251 at night) and om_Room-24.

F/J electric two-stage pleated shades and blue-LED button: verified. OMAAT, LALF and TPG all describe one press for the sheer and a second for the blackout. The split pill with a blue ring and a pinhole below, centred on the sill, matches om_Room-24 almost exactly. The horizontal pleat stripes match. The photo pleat pitch is about 14 mm (about 30 pleats over the opening) against 11 mm in the model. The blackout shows moire at oblique distance.

PY/Y manual shade, stowed: the photo shows a tall cream band about 0.04 m deep at the top of the opening. That is the shade's bottom edge with a flat, wide grip lip in the bezel colour (grip #9c957a in shadow, bezel #c7c0ab). The render shows only a thin light-grey line (0.016 m).

Dado and air-return grilles: the planar sloped slate facet with one rounded grille per bay and a white placard matches py_37301. The photo has about 30 horizontal slats and 7 internal vertical ribs (8 bays). The render ribs are bright white lines (they sit 5.8 mm proud and catch light), while the photo ribs are slat-toned. The grille reads too dark in the cabin: #23293a to #293044 against the photo's #454b5e. The dado turns saturated blue (#2a406e in s04) against the photo's slate #515d72, whose saturation is about 29 % against about 62 % in the render.

Carpets and Y track covers: the Y aisle carpet now renders #374461 against the photo's #36445f (y_47301), a match. The blue track covers read right. The carpet near the wall in s04 is #1a202f, crushed by AO against the photo's #515f76 (py_37301).
Door-area floor: renders light grey #a0a5ad. The ANA door-2 galley and door areas show a dark mottled grey floor (#676367 galley, #4a433b at the door).

Type A door linings and surrounds: the render is a flat panel with a heavy 12 mm black outline, a large window at the cabin-window height (1.13 m), a low flat 0.36 m bustle and a red flag at 1.62 m. The real ANA door (sp_py_09) is different. A large protruding off-white slide bustle runs from the floor to about 0.8 m with a ledge. A panel with the red arming arc sits at about 1.0-1.3 m. There is a small viewing window high up at about 1.5-1.7 m, forward of centre. The door edge reads as a thin shadow line, not black.

Window light on the wall: each open window throws a pale rectangle about 0.45 m wide with hard vertical edges onto the sidewall, cutting the blue band. In s05 the row y=160 steps from #9ea9db to #c3cbe5 within about 20 px at x 380-420, and from #b1bbe0 to #8391d5 at x 820-840. It reads as a sticker. Sun patches on the seats are elongated streaks, which is plausible.

issues.detail: 777 window recess too short, too narrow and centred on the pane
issues.problem: Real 777 recesses are tall tubs that reach the bin line, with the bezel in the lower part and narrow piers between them. The render recess stops 0.20 m above the bezel and 0.11 m below it, and is 0.39 m wide, so the wall reads as a generic airliner wall.
issues.evidence: y_47303 (head-on): recess 175 px wide, bezel 115 px, pitch about 220 px, so recess/pitch 0.80 and recess/bezel 1.52 (0.46 m if the bezel is 0.305). Recess top is 150 px above the bezel top, about 0.40 m, and just under the bins. Bottom is about 90 px below, about 0.24 m. sp_py_13 (crop c_py13) gives the same numbers: recess/bezel width 1.52, 0.40 m above, 0.21-0.28 m below. Render s03: recess/pitch 0.76, recess top 0.39 bezel-heights above the bezel against 0.9 in the photo, bottom 0.30 against 0.54, recess h/w 1.98 against 2.35.
issues.fix: src/07_shell.js: REC = { hw: 0.222, top: 0.455, bot: -0.47, rTop: 0.13, rBot: 0.11, depth: 0.040, btn: -0.30 }. The recess then spans v 0.66-1.585 (top at the bin line vTop 1.60) and is 0.444 m wide, leaving 0.089 m piers. Keep the cell band enclosing it: WALL.vb0 0.74 -> 0.60, WALL.vb1 1.58 -> 1.595, WALL.bottomRows [0,0.05,0.33,0.37,0.40,0.50,0.60]. Move the btn on the sill down with the bot and keep it 0.03 m inside the recess floor. Optionally deepen the recess towards the top: map ring depth d -> d + 0.02*smoothstep(0.1, 0.45, dv) in windowParts' map for the lip/floor rings so the upper recess face darkens as in sp_py_13 (recess upper face #9c9791 against wall #bdb8b3, 0.82).

issues.detail: Door linings do not look like a 777 Type A door (the door window lives in 07_shell; the lining furniture is in 10_mono, the monuments owner)
issues.problem: The door window sits at the cabin-window height and is nearly cabin-window size. The slide bustle is a low, flat 0.36 m panel. The red flag is at 1.62 m. The door gap is a heavy black outline.
issues.evidence: sp_py_09 (crop c_door, FA about 1.6 m tall for scale): bustle from the floor to about 0.80 m, off-white, protruding, with a ledge on top. Red arming arc panel at about 1.0-1.3 m. Small viewing window about 0.2 m square at about 1.5-1.7 m on the forward half. Header at about 1.9 m. Render s06/s07: window centre about 1.13 m, black 12 mm gap lines.
issues.fix: 07_shell.js buildShell door surrounds: dp = windowCellPattern(cellW, 0.20, 0.26, 0.05, 1.55) (window centre 1.55 m, small), and pass topRows [1.72, 1.80, 1.90, 2.02] so the cell band encloses it. The glass for the door hole is wherever that is built; match it. 10_mono.js door linings: slide bustle gRBox(0.10,0.36,0.92) at v 0.30 -> gRBox(0.16, 0.78, 0.92, 0.05, 2) centred at v 0.42 plus a 0.03 m ledge at 0.82. Move the red flag from v 1.62 to a 0.28 m red arc/indicator at v 1.15 on the aft half. MAT.doorGap 12 mm #2a2d31 -> 5 mm #6f6c66.

issues.detail: Hard-edged window-glow rectangles on the sidewall (lighting area: 04_shaders.js; visible on the shell)
issues.problem: The reveal term (u_winGlow * wl.rgb * reveal * 1.4) uses the window LUT alpha, which spans each window in z with step edges, times a y band. It paints a pale rectangle about 0.45 m wide with vertical edges round every open window, and cuts the blue band.
issues.evidence: s05 row y=160: #9ea9db -> #c3cbe5 in about 20 px at x 380-420, and #b1bbe0 -> #8391d5 at x 820-840. Same pale block in s01 and s08. No photo shows such a block (sp_py_13, y_47303).
issues.fix: Lighting owner: feather the LUT in z (sample with LINEAR filtering and write alpha with a 0.08 m cosine falloff past each window's +-0.22 m), or replace the rectangle mask with the recess shape: reveal *= 1 - smoothstep(-0.02, 0.03, sdRecess(dz, dy)) in GLSL, using REC from 07_shell. Keep the glow inside the recess, fading over about 5 cm.

issues.problem: The door and cross-aisle floors (MAT.vinyl) render light grey. ANA's door and galley floors are dark mottled grey.
issues.evidence: sp_py_09: galley floor #676367, door-area floor #4a433b. Render s06 floor #a0a5ad, s07 similar.
issues.fix: MAT.vinyl { c: '#8d9096' } -> { c: '#5e5b5f', r: 0.6, l: LAYER.vinyl }, and check that the vinyl layer carries a low-contrast mottle.

issues.detail: Stowed manual shade reads as a thin grey line
issues.problem: With the shade up, PY/Y windows should show a tall cream band at the top of the opening: the shade bottom plus a wide grip in the bezel colour.
issues.evidence: sp_py_24 crop c_py24: band about 0.09 of the opening height (about 0.04 m), colour about the bezel colour (#c7c0ab; grip underside #9c957a). Render s03: 0.016 m light-grey lip, MAT.shadeRail #c4c2bc.
issues.fix: shadeRailGeo('manual'): gRBox(SHADE.w, 0.016, 0.014, ...) -> gRBox(SHADE.w, 0.026, 0.018, 0.008, 1) using MAT.shade (#e2e0da), with the finger scoop kept darker (#a9a7a1). shadeMats: manual railY = lerp(top - 0.020, ...) -> lerp(top - 0.036, ...) so about 0.036 m of panel plus grip stays visible when stowed.

issues.detail: Dado grille contrast wrong: white ribs, near-black louvres, over-saturated dado
issues.problem: The ribs render as bright white bars, the louvre field is too dark, and the dado turns saturated blue under the cabin light.
issues.evidence: py_37301 crop c_grille: ribs the same tone as the slats (grille average #454b5e, dado #515d72, 29 % saturation). Render s04 dado #2a406e (about 62 % saturation), grille #293044. s02 grille #23293a. win_low/c_rgrille: white ribs.
issues.fix: Ribs: push them to depth 0.0045 (behind the slat front edge at 0.0055) and give them their own material { c: '#586079', r: 0.6 } instead of MAT.grille. WMAT.grilleBack '#1c212c' -> '#2b3140'. MAT.dado '#6c7690' -> '#6f7686' (desaturated; the lighting owner should check that the bounce/hemiBot blue isn't tinting the floor-level dado). MAT.grille '#707b96' -> '#737a8c'.

issues.detail: Pleat pitch slightly fine, and moire on the blackout at oblique distance
issues.problem: 40 pleats at 11 mm with a baked valley/crest colour alternation per row alias into diagonal moire.
issues.evidence: om_Business-Class-The-Room-24: about 30 pleats over the opening (FFT of a column crop gives a period of 28.6 px over 800 px), about 14 mm. win_oblique: leftmost blackout shows diagonal moire.
issues.fix: shadePanelGeo: n = 80 -> 62 (31 pleats, about 14 mm). Soften the baked stripe from x0.86 to x0.90 and let the zig-zag normals carry the stripes.

issues.detail: Open seam where the J dado profile meets door zones (in-progress THE Room fix)
issues.problem: wallGrid only inserts the DADO/DADO_J step when a J boundary falls strictly inside zs. Where a J zone ends at a run end (a door-zone boundary), the J dado starts at x 2.862 but the door surround's bottom rows use DADO (x 2.70). That leaves an uncapped triangular slot, up to 0.16 m deep and 0.40 m tall, visible from the cross-aisle if not hidden by a monument.
issues.evidence: src/07_shell.js wallGrid: condition b + d > zs[0] + 1e-4 && b + d < zs[last] - 1e-4. Door surrounds call wallGrid without g.jz.
issues.fix: In buildShell, for each J range end [a, b] that coincides with a run end, add a cap strip: for v in WALL.bottomRows (<= 0.40) push wallAt(v, DADO) and wallAt(v, DADO_J) at z = a (or b), triangulate, fixWinding, MAT.dado. Alternatively give the door-surround wallGrid the same jz so its bottom rows follow DADO_J near J zones. Also check THE Suite zones (cls 'F') for the same footwell intrusion (q03).

questionsForUser: Do you have (or can you take) a photo of an ANA 777-300ER Type A door from the cabin side? The only real door image found is a small, distant shot in a SANspotter PY review (sp_py_09): window high on the forward half, tall slide bustle. A clear photo would pin down the door-window height and size.

Real photos put the recess top right at the bins, 0.40 m above the bezel. With the pane centre at 1.13 m and the bins at 1.60 m, the model only has 0.25 m there. Is the pane-centre height 1.13 m sourced? If not, would you accept lowering CAB.win.yc to about 1.06 m (and the grille/dado stays), or raising the bin line (ceiling/bins owner)?

Should the daylight QA views use the blue boarding/cruise mood at all? SANspotter's boarding photo (sp_y_12) confirms a blue wash on the upper sidewall, but ANA's official photos, which the QA pairs use, show white walls.
